# Proposal 3 · §11–16 Interaction → cross-platform

DESIGN PROPOSAL · PART 3 OF 5 · §11–16

## 11 Interaction model

Each intent has one primary gesture per device, taken from OS conventions, and every action is also a visible control and a ⌘K command. Nothing depends on memorising a gesture.

| Intent | Mouse | Trackpad | Keyboard | Touch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Turn page** | Wheel notch; click in margin | One swipe, either axis = one page | → ← Space ⇧Space PgDn PgUp | Tap side zone; swipe |
| **Scroll** (Scroll mode) | Wheel | Two fingers | ↑ ↓ Space | Drag |
| **Open TOC** | List button | List button | ⌘T · chapters ⌥↑ ⌥↓ | Centre tap → list button |
| **Search** | Search button | Search button | ⌘F | Centre tap → search button |
| **Select text** | Drag; double- / triple-click | Drag; force-click Look Up | F7 caret, ⇧ + arrows | Long-press, drag handles |
| **Highlight** | Colour in selection bar | Colour in selection bar | H or ⇧⌘H | Colour in edit menu or bar |
| **Add note** | Note in bar; right-click › Add note | Note in bar | N or ⇧⌘N | Note in edit menu or bar |
| **Open settings** | Aa button | Aa button | ⌘+ ⌘− directly; ⌘K › Reading settings | Centre tap → Aa |
| **Hide interface** | Turn page; move away | Turn page | Esc | Centre tap |

**Where devices converge:** the same surfaces, the same button order, the same shortcuts on hardware keyboards and the same one-layer rule. **Where they differ on purpose:** touch uses tap zones, bottom sheets and the system edit menu; desktop uses edge reveal, margin click targets and anchored popovers. A click inside text on desktop never turns a page, because on desktop clicks begin selections; a tap inside text on touch does, because on touch selection begins with a long-press. On touch laptops the rule is chosen per event from the pointer type, while layout density stays fixed so the screen never jumps.

## 12 Keyboard-first experience

| Action | macOS | Windows / Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Next / previous page | → ← · Space ⇧Space · PgDn PgUp | Same |
| Next / previous chapter | ⌥↓ · ⌥↑ (also ] [) | Alt+↓ · Alt+↑ (also ] [) |
| Search in book | ⌘F | Ctrl+F |
| Next / previous result | ⌘G · ⇧⌘G | F3 · ⇧F3 |
| Contents | ⌘T | Ctrl+T |
| Go to location | ⌘J | Ctrl+J |
| Highlights and notes panel | ⇧⌘A | Ctrl+Shift+A |
| Highlight / note on selection | ⇧⌘H / ⇧⌘N (also H / N) | Ctrl+Shift+H / Ctrl+Shift+N (also H / N) |
| Move into the selection bar | F6 | F6 |
| Text size larger / smaller / reset | ⌘+ · ⌘− · ⌘0 | Ctrl + · Ctrl − · Ctrl 0 |
| Command palette | ⌘K | Ctrl+K |
| Back after a jump | ⌘[ | Alt+← |
| Library | ⌘L | Ctrl+L |
| Full screen | ⌃⌘F | F11 |
| Close layer / hide chrome | Esc | Esc |

**Single-key shortcuts** (H, N, [, ]) are conveniences, never the only way: each has a modified equivalent, they act only when the page has focus and no text field is active, and one setting turns them all off (WCAG 2.1.4). They switch off automatically while a screen reader is running, because readers such as NVDA and JAWS use single letters for their own navigation. Chapter keys use ⌥ + arrows because [ and ] need AltGr on many European layouts; shortcuts bind to physical key positions. Every shortcut is shown next to its command in ⌘K and on a cheat sheet opened with ?. Esc never leaves the book. Remapping is deferred, and extensions cannot claim core shortcuts.

## 13 Visual design system

The metaphor is **paper and ink**: warm neutral grounds, ink-coloured text and one accent — burnt sienna #8C4A2F (Night #D39A73) — kept for focus, the active state and progress S4.

| Element | Rule |
|---|---|
| Type | Reading: the book’s font or Literata. UI: the platform face (SF Pro, Segoe UI Variable, the desktop sans on Linux); the comps use Instrument Sans as a stand-in. Only three UI sizes — 12, 14, 17 px — and weights 400/500/600. |
| Spacing | 4 px base: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64. |
| Borders | 1 px hairlines at about 10% ink, only where a surface meets the page. Buttons have no borders. |
| Shadows | Popovers and floating panels only. The page and docked panels have none. |
| Radius | 6 px controls, 10 px popovers and cards, 14 px sheets, round for colour dots and chips. |
| Icons | 1.6 px outline strokes on a 24 px grid; filled only when active. |
| Hover | A 6% ink wash behind the control; the icon itself doesn’t change colour. |
| Focus and selected states | A 2 px accent ring with 2 px offset on :focus-visible — never removed. Selected tabs, segments, swatches and switches also carry a border or outline (≥ 3:1), never only a shadow or tint, so they survive Windows high-contrast mode. |
| Minimum size | 12 px for any UI text a reader must read or act on; decorative cover lettering is hidden from assistive tech because the title repeats below it. |
| Disabled | 40% opacity in menus. In contextual bars, unavailable actions are hidden rather than greyed out. |
| Overlays | Popovers and docked panels have no scrim; modals use a 20% scrim of the page colour, not black. |

**Blend in or stand out.** Controls that serve reading blend in: the bars share the page background, icons use secondary ink, and the location line is caption-sized. Controls that commit or interrupt get strong affordance: the ink-coloured selection bar, the Resume button, permission prompts, and destructive and recovery actions.

## 14 Motion and transitions

| Transition | Duration | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Chrome show / hide | 160 ms in, 220 ms out | Fade with a 4 px slide from its edge |
| Navigator open / close | 220 ms | Slides from the left; the column recentres by transform and reflows only afterwards |
| Popover | 140 ms | Grows from 98% out of its anchor |
| Selection bar | 100 ms | Fade only, after mouse-up |
| Page turn by key, wheel or trackpad | 0 ms | Instant; an optional 120 ms crossfade in Preferences |
| Page turn by swipe | Tracks the finger, 180 ms settle | No bounce |
| Jump to result or annotation | Instant + 1.2 s pulse | The pulse orients you; no scrolling across pages |
| Theme change | 200 ms | Crossfade |
| Library → book | 240 ms | The cover grows into the page |

No transition in the reader lasts more than 250 ms. Motion is removed entirely when the OS asks for reduced motion (everything becomes a fade of 100 ms or less), during key-repeat page turns, and for page turns while a screen reader is running.

## 15 Accessibility

Accessibility is a constraint the minimalism has to satisfy, not a layer added later. The reconciliation is **quiet visuals, generous behaviour**: small icons with 44 px hit areas, hidden chrome that focus reveals, and calm colours that still pass AAA.

| Area | Design |
|---|---|
| Keyboard | Every function is reachable. Focus order: top bar → Navigator → page → bottom bar. Tab from the immersive page reveals the chrome and focuses its first control, so nothing is ever focused while invisible. Focus is trapped only in modals. |
| Screen readers | The page is the book’s own semantic HTML (headings, lists, language, alt text). Pagination is visual only: assistive tech reads the chapter continuously, and **the visible page follows the reading position**, so low-vision readers who listen and look stay in sync. Page-turn announcements are brief and can be turned off. Icon buttons have labels and tooltips. EPUB accessibility metadata appears in Book info. |
| Focus indicator | The 2 px accent ring — the one decoration that is never removed. |
| Contrast | Body text ≥ 7:1 in every theme (AAA); secondary UI text ≥ 4.5:1; highlighted text ≥ 9:1. Non-text marks that carry meaning — highlight underlines, search outlines, switch borders, focus rings — are ≥ 3:1 against the page. |
| Timing | Nothing that offers an action disappears on a timer the reader can’t control: messages last 10 s, pause on hover or focus, and remain in ⌘K › Recently closed. |
| Text spacing | User-applied letter, word, line and paragraph spacing (WCAG 1.4.12) triggers re-pagination instead of clipping. |
| Text scaling | The OS text size is the base; reader text goes to 48 px; at large sizes margins shrink before lines get short; the chrome follows the OS setting. |
| Reduced motion | See §14. |
| Touch targets | 44 × 44 pt on iPad, 48 dp elsewhere; hit areas extend past the visible icon. |
| High zoom | At 200–400% the layout switches to its narrow form: one column, floating panels, no horizontal scrolling in the UI. |
| Forced colours | Windows high-contrast mode is honoured; highlights fall back to system highlight colours. |

## 16 Cross-platform design

**Identical everywhere:** layout, surfaces, themes, reading behaviour, gesture thresholds, the logical shortcut set and the state model. **Native per platform:** everything the OS has already taught its users.

| Aspect | macOS | Windows | Linux | iPad / tablets |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Window | Traffic lights in an integrated title bar that hides with the chrome | Caption buttons at right, integrated title bar | Decorations follow the desktop’s button layout | No window chrome |
| Menus | Full menu bar with every command | No menu bar; ⋯ app menu + Ctrl+K | As Windows | System edit menu; hold ⌘ for shortcut overlay |
| Modifier | ⌘; Back ⌘[ | Ctrl; Back Alt+← | Ctrl; Back Alt+← | ⌘ with a hardware keyboard |
| Trackpad | Gesture phases detect momentum | Precision-touchpad heuristics | Toolkit / libinput events | — |
| Opening files | Open With; drop on Dock icon | File association; Jump List of recent books | MIME registration in the .desktop file | Files app and share sheet |
| Full screen | ⌃⌘F, own Space | F11 | F11 | Always |
| Theme | Follows appearance | Follows system; high contrast honoured | Follows the portal colour scheme | Follows system |

**Touch-enabled laptops** choose behaviour per event (a touch tap in text turns the page, a mouse click selects) without switching layout mid-session. **Implementation note:** because EPUB is HTML and CSS, a web rendering core inside a thin native shell (Tauri, for example) gives the same layout everywhere. The cost is engine differences — WebKit on macOS and Linux, Chromium-based WebView2 on Windows — which the renderer must test against.
